dispositions.topic_text: Concrete Python runtime artifact identified and compared by the required digest
dispositions.what: The release process's concrete identifier and comparison for this (Python artifact digest; release identity and its immutability); every option keeps: a mismatch prevents the release from starting, and the same release gives the same list.
keeps:
2. A running instance uses exactly those; installing a dependency whose digest
   differs fails.
options: Digest a named Python distribution or source archive
Digest a canonical complete installed runtime tree
Represent Python as a constituent fixed by the base-image digest
consequences: The deployment specification must identify one comparison subject unambiguously so every verifier reaches the same installation result while preserving the separate Python-version-and-digest obligation.

dispositions.topic_text: Definition and immutability of release identity across installations
dispositions.what: The release process's concrete identifier and comparison for this (Python artifact digest; release identity and its immutability); every option keeps: a mismatch prevents the release from starting, and the same release gives the same list.
keeps: 3. A dependency changes only by a new release, verified as any release.
options: A permanent release identifier defines identity and may never be rebound
An immutable release-manifest or artifact digest defines identity, making changed contents a new release despite reuse of an external label
A version plus a signed manifest digest defines identity and changed contents require a new pair
consequences: Deployment must define identity and rebinding consistently so installing the same release always yields the same dependency list and changed dependencies constitute a new verified release.

dispositions.topic_text: Whether an immutable base-image digest satisfies the exact-version requirement
dispositions.reason: Judged before (round-111 T5, carried to deploy): what counts as an exact version of each kind is the release process's representation, outside Registry (A20 rule 5).
